title: Claude made a trailer for my game, wdyt?
author: TW0b14S
selftext:
I'm building this steampunk sailing RPG (Rust/Bevy) with an AI agent loop — it writes the code, plays the game, files its own bugs. I asked it for a trailer and it handed me 8 seconds of a boat going in a straight line, because it had no director's tools: the camera could only teleport, the day/night clock races, the sea monster spawns invisibly deep, lightning lasts 0.16s, and screen-recording dies when the machine auto-locks.

So it spent some time building itself a camera department — scriptable camera moves, a hold on time-of-day, a way to summon and surface the leviathan, lightning it can freeze, a clean HUD-free lens, and a native frame recorder that works even with the screen locked — shipped as six issues across two reviewed + merged PRs with tests. Then it shot the reel above from a script of API calls.

What do you think about the trailer? Producing materials for marketing is super important but also a major drag (imho). Will we be able to go full auto on marketing using agents?

Full write-up + how each piece works: [https://h0bb3.github.io/log](https://h0bb3.github.io/log)

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body: to elaborate: Bevy (an ECS engine) for the core, but the rendering is all custom-written WGSL: a spectral FFT ocean, an SDF island generator, mesh clouds, closed-form weather. No Unity/Unreal.

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: As a trailer, it’s pretty bad—it doesn’t show much (or hardly anything) about the game. The game itself might actually be cool, but the trailer simply doesn’t show that.

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body: Yeah I agree 😬 I think Claude just wanted to show the functionality of the camera API with this one. Not so much the game itself.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: You can ask for much more complex camera work and shots, you had a good idea but I say you gotta challenge Claude more. I've thing in like to do with Claude is ask it to do another pass on it's work to improve it (like if I ask for a mesh or shader or cutscene/animation)

comments.author: True-Explorer-9701
comments.body: i think some kind of gameplay will be good to be involved.

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body: Indeed, giving Claude free hand made it show the new camera API it had invented and not the game itself.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body:
probably context preference, it tends to think about what it recently thought about.  I would change the 6-8 section area to include the ship or whale moving towards the island.

I'd actually have the AI redo the entire thing.  Go director mode first, use AI to help storyboard the trailer.  

[www.adventuresincausality.com](http://www.adventuresincausality.com) has a game development guide that can help you and the AI design the trailer.

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body: Thanks, will check it out!

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: [https://github.com/adventuresincausality/game-development-constitution](https://github.com/adventuresincausality/game-development-constitution) might be easier, especially if you point your AI at it.  Is structured so the AI only loads the context it needs.

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body:
It invented an API so it could control the camera in the game, trigger certain events etc. Then it did the video, not sure how it did the last info screen but Claude has its ways I suppose.

Running it on a Linux machine so I guess it has a lot of low level video libs at its disposal for doing editing.

replies.author: TW0b14S

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body: Totally agree!

comments.author: rednoodles
comments.body: I think trailers are pretty easy and it'd be better do to on your own. There's 2 good rules from filmmaking to utilize, the 3 second frame rule (change frames every 3-4 seconds) and the 60/30/10 color split rule. Use some actual gameplay. And use AI for the voice/music overlay.

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body: Good advice, wonder how much these models know about stuff like that. Well... Def more than I do 😂

replies.author: rednoodles
replies.body: I think it does a decent job in your video, it just needs gameplay in it. You could have it write a script perhaps to go by, and get suggestions from it on what type of gameplay you should show that best describes your game.

comments.author: oVerde
comments.body:
Stop! ✋

Dont make me believe in it then sink a month of hours and tokens trying it and not getting even close to the posted results.

replies.author: TW0b14S
replies.body: Well getting the game to the state it is in has taken several weeks (full details in my linked dev log) but the camera API and doing the reel itself took maybe an hour or so. Granted the result is pretty bad 😅 the API is there and making the next reel is cheaper. I guess this is somewhat the gist of AI it is not genius but relentless and will just keep going until target is achieved 🤔😛
